title: Wolff (The Hague) to Wilhelmina of Prussia, Princess of Orange, 25 Jul 1801 (KHA Wilhelmina Prinses van Pruisen inv. 192; DECODE R2232)

documents.shelfmark: Koninklijk Huisarchief, The Hague, Wilhelmina Prinses van Pruisen (A32), inv. 192; DECODE R2232
documents.route: Wolff (The Hague) -> Wilhelmina, Princess of Orange (London)

plaintext.source: No decipherment on the DECODE images or record.

transcription.source: DECODE IMG_R2232_I15506-15508, rotated, cut into bands
transcription.notes: Counted with grep over ct.txt number groups (the --measure tool also counts the clear words kept in capitals: 1416 tokens).

system.summary: Numbers 1-45 with superscript index 1-4: row N lists four consecutive values of one running sequence of fractions, digits and letters; the index picks one. Up to four homophones per letter.
system.sibling_key: DECODE R2233, Wolff's letter of 8 Sept 1801 sending the key; used directly.
system.notes: Accented letters à, ô, û have their own values; the vowels a e i o u repeat after z, giving them extra homophones.

prior_solution.where: DECODE status non-decrypted; R2233 note describes the system but gives no reading

conditions.human_role: Project-level: DECODE login cookie supplied, problem posed with /goal. No target-specific intervention.

solution.what: Fetched R2232 (3 images) and the next record R2233 with the session cookie; R2233 is Wolff's covering letter of 8 Sept 1801 with the key.
Transcribed the R2233 key: 45 rows of four consecutive values of one sequence (0 1/8 1/4 1/2 1..9 à a..z with ô, û, then a e i o u a); group = row number + superscript index.
Tested the key on the ciphered year/place and signature of image 1: 'en 1791, à Berlin', 'Wolff'.
Transcribed all three pages (1,065 groups, 119 distinct) from rotated full-resolution bands; found page order P2, P3, P1.
Decoded mechanically; corrected a few one-place slips from context into reading.txt.

outcome.method_basis: The key is on the next DECODE record, R2233, at the same inventory number: Wolff's own covering letter of 8 Sept 1801 sending 'la clef ci-jointe' for the 25 July letter; it decoded the letter on the first pass.
outcome.notes: Every group has a value; a few one-place slips corrected from context; two clear passages summarised, not transcribed.
